main_issue: This boundary describes an evidentiary holding queue, not a coherent vulnerability mechanism. No representative cases are listed, and every mechanism dimension (source shape, sink, missing guard, exploit precondition, safe fix) is 'needs per-case evidence.' The cases share only that they lack sufficient source review — they may not share the same path-traversal submechanism at all. As a semantic guideline, it has no mechanism-level content to judge.

The two representative cases share a coherent core mechanism: attacker-controlled path fragments are resolved beneath a base directory and then used for filesystem operations (create, read, write, delete, list, metadata) without first normalizing or canonicalizing the resolved path and verifying it stays under the intended root. DSpace demonstrates this through upload temp directory and chunk path construction from request parameters; S3Proxy demonstrates it through object key and prefix resolution under a container root. The boundary text accurately captures the source shape, sink effects, missing guard, exploit precondition, and safe fix semantics across both cases. No revision needed.
